column1: # Every architecture the OpenWrt buildbot publishes, with a target that builds
# it and the emulator to run it under.
# Columns: arch, target, qemu program, cpu model.
# The cpu model is always named, never left to the emulator's default. The
# default 32-bit PowerPC model does not implement isel, and musl for
# powerpc_8548 (CPU_TYPE 8548, the e500v2 core in parts such as the P1010) holds
# 63 of them, so the C library faults with an illegal instruction before
# reaching main, whatever the package holds. That reads exactly like a package
# failure and is not one. Naming the model removes the guesswork.
# Each model here was checked by running that target's own musl loader under it.
# Where the exact CPU is absent from qemu-user, the closest superset is used, on
# the reasoning that too weak a model invents failures while too rich a model
# hides them and skews runtime feature detection:
#   arm_cortex-a5_vfpv4   cortex-a7   no cortex-a5 in qemu-user
#   arm_xscale            arm926      no xscale or pxa model
#   armeb_xscale          arm926      likewise, big endian
#   powerpc_464fp         460exb      the 460 family model
# The x86 models are composed from features rather than picked from the list,
# because every stock model is richer than the part its target names, and a
# richer model hides a fault instead of finding one. What each target asks for:
#   i386_pentium-mmx      pentium,+mmx      MMX, no SSE, no CMOV
#   i386_pentium4         pentium3,+sse2    SSE2, no SSE3, no SSSE3
#   x86_64                Opteron_G1,-sse3  the Opteron 240 of 2003, earliest
#                                           stepping, so SSE2 and nothing above
# Each boundary was confirmed by running a one-instruction program under the
# model and requiring the illegal-instruction fault. The stock choices were all
# too rich: pentium2 grants CMOV, which a Geode has not; n270 grants SSSE3, so
# that job selected the SSSE3 path and never ran the SSE2 one a Pentium 4 uses;
# and the emulator's own x86_64 default grants SSE3. An assumption of SSSE3
# that faults on AMD K8 and K10 survived years of CI on hosts that all had it,
# which is the whole argument for naming the floor rather than a typical part.
# x86 has four subtargets and three package architectures: geode and legacy
# both fall to the i386 default of pentium-mmx, so one row covers the pair.
# The fifth column names an instruction set to assert, or "-" for none. Two
# architectures use it, in opposite directions, and each pairing is deliberate.
# arm_fa526 asks for "v4", and is held to no more than that.
# That target compiles to plain ARMv4, which has no bx and so cannot enter Thumb
# code: its binaries hold no bx or blx at all, where the ARMv5 build of the same
# package holds 133. qemu-user always maps a Thumb vdso, so under an ARMv4 or
# ARMv5 model the call to __vdso_gettimeofday runs Thumb bytes in ARM state and
# branches into the weeds. Real hardware never meets this, because the Linux ARM
# vdso needs ARMv7 and a gemini kernel supplies none, leaving musl on plain
# syscalls. The currently shipped package fails the same way, so it is nothing
# this repository changed, and qemu-user offers no way to withhold the vdso.
# Skipping the architecture would leave a hole, and simply naming a richer model
# could hide a real mismatch. So it runs under cortex-a7, which can interwork,
# and isa-check.sh holds the binaries to ARMv4 in the same job. The emulator
# then proves the code runs, and the check proves the code is what the target
# asks for.
# powerpc_8548 asks for "spe", and is held to containing it. The e500v2 core
# does the tile XOR 64 bits at a time through its SPE unit, and GCC has dropped
# SPE support, so that path is hand-written assembly reached by a build flag
# rather than by a macro the compiler defines. udpspeeder-simd reads the -mcpu
# the target passes and sets the flag itself. Nothing a packet test can observe
# changes if that reading ever breaks: the tunnel still passes traffic, on the
# slower word path. Requiring the opcodes is what makes the loss audible. This
# assertion applies to udpspeeder-simd alone, the stock package having no SPE
# path to lose.
# riscv64_riscv64 and mips_4kec have package directories on the buildbot but are
# frozen leftovers, not live architectures: they were last built in April and
# July of 2025 against zlib 1.3.1, where a live architecture carries a build
# from this month. riscv64_riscv64 is the name the release branches use for
# riscv64_generic, and nothing in the tree sets CPU_TYPE to 4kec.
# armeb_xscale is omitted. Its target is XScale and qemu-armeb models only
# arm926 and arm1176, so the binary meets an instruction the model lacks and
# faults. Upstream's own udpspeeder fails the same way here, so this is the
# emulator's reach, not the package. The feed still builds and serves it.
